messages.content: You debug code by reading it carefully and finding logical errors.

message.content:
# Bug Found

The issue is on **line 4**. When a new maximum is found, the code incorrectly assigns `arr[0]` instead of `arr[i]`.

## The Problem

```js
if (max < arr[i]) max = arr[0];  // ❌ Wrong - always assigns first element
```

## The Fix

```js
if (max < arr[i]) max = arr[i];  // ✅ Correct - assigns current element
```

## Explanation

| What was written | What it should be | Why it matters |
|------------------|-------------------|----------------|
| `max = arr[0]` | `max = arr[i]` | `arr[0]` is always the first element, so `max` never actually updates to hold a new maximum value |

The condition `max < arr[i]` correctly identifies when a larger value is found, but then the assignment uses the wrong variable—it should store `arr[i]` (the current element being compared), not `arr[0]` (the first element).
